# The three absorber papers the patent cites instead of Landy

**Research date:** 2026-09-08
**Ticket:** [#246](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/246) — generated by [#142](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/142); informs [#116](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/116) and [#232](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/232). Part of [#104](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/104).
**Question:** US12089385B2's Example 3 reproduces Landy et al. 2008's dimensions digit for digit but reports it at ~9.2 GHz where Landy measured 11.5 GHz. The patent never cites Landy. Is one of the three absorber papers it *does* cite the source of FIG. 7G's curve?

Provenance tags are `CONTEXT.md`'s ladder. Every source below was retrieved this session; §5 lists what could not be.

---

## Bottom line up front

**1. No. All three are excluded, and none is close.** The composite hypothesis — Landy's dimension table paired with somebody else's response curve — finds no support in the papers the patent actually cites.

**2. The hypothesis rested on a premise that turns out to be false.** #246 asserted the three papers are cited "precisely where a reader would expect the source of the design to be named." They are not. The patent cites them in a generic *"see, e.g."* for **embodiments it did not build**, one sentence after stating what Example 3 actually is. §1.

**3. All three cite Landy.** Gu at ref 9 of 28, Ghosh at ref 3 of 31, Singh at ref 1 of 19 — each verified by DOI in publisher-deposited metadata, not by name-matching. And **Gu et al. are Duke ECE, Landy's own department.** The patent says all three are *"incorporated by reference in their entireties,"* so Landy enters the document transitively while being absent from its own reference list. §4.

**4. The `ε₀` vs `ε₀ε_r` side-check came back negative.** Ghosh does not cite Tretyakov & Simovski 2003 and does not restate Costa's thin-spacer correction. [#234](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/234) is unchanged: still two published statements, still 1.487× apart. §6.

**5. A records failure surfaced that is worth more than the exclusions.** Two of the three author lists this repo held for these papers were invented, under a label claiming they came verbatim from the patent — which prints no author lists at all. Corrected; `RUNNING-LISTS.md` §3 correction 44. §7.

*In plain terms: we asked whether the patent copied its absorption curve from one of the three papers it points at. It did not — none of them even operates at the right frequency with the right kind of device — and the sentence we thought was pointing at the design's source turns out to be pointing somewhere else entirely.*

---

## 1. The citing sentence is not a provenance statement

Read directly from `knowledge/corpus/us_patent_12089385B2.txt`, lines 1020–1027. `LITERATURE-SUPPORTED`:

> "By combining the two different shapes (i.e., electric ring resonator (ERR) in the top and wire resonator in the bottom), the electric resonance and magnetic resonance can be tuned to overlap each other which results in no reflected signal.
>
> **In other embodiments, the functional inserts might also include other combinations such as electrically coupled LC resonator (ELC) and split ring resonators (SRRs)**, and their variations can also be used to create absorption surface. **See, e.g.,** Gu et al. […]; Ghosh et al. […], and Singh et al. […], herein incorporated by reference in their entireties."

The first sentence states what Example 3 **is**: ERR on top, wire resonator underneath. The second gestures at *other* topologies — ELC and SRR — that the patent explicitly did **not** use, and hangs the three citations off that, followed by drafting boilerplate.

So the three papers are cited as **alternatives the patent did not build**, not as the source of what it did build. #246's framing — and #142's characterisation of the citations as sitting "precisely where a reader would expect the source of the design to be named" — was wrong.

**This is #246's own stated counterweight, visible on the page:** *citation is not derivation*. It was written into the ticket as a caution and turned out to be the answer.

---

## 2. Gu — excluded decisively, on full text

**Gu, Barrett, Hand, Popa & Cummer**, "A broadband low-reflection metamaterial absorber," *J. Appl. Phys.* **108**(6), 064913 (2010). DOI [10.1063/1.3485808](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3485808). **Duke University, Dept. of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Center for Metamaterials and Integrated Plasmonics.**

Open access (Unpaywall: `is_oa: true`, green). **Full published text read** — the strongest evidentiary basis of the three.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Peak near 9.2 GHz? | **No.** *"a maximum absorption of 99.9% at 2.4 GHz"*; also 2.65, 2.67, 2.74 GHz. Nearest is **3.83× away** |
| Metallisation | **0.017 mm** — *"The copper traces are simulated to be 0.017 mm thick"*. Landy's 17 µm, not the patent's 0.15 mm |
| Shared dimensions | **None.** ELC `a1=0.35, a2=1, a3=0` mm; SRR `b1=0.7, b2=3, b3=0.5` mm. FR4 0.2 mm, **εr 4.4** (patent asserts 4.8), tanδ **never stated** (absence verified in full text) |
| Cites Landy? | **Yes**, ref 9 of 28, discussed twice in prose |

Two independent exclusions beyond the frequency gap:

- **The apparatus forecloses it.** *"measurements were taken on a WR340 closed waveguide between 2–3 GHz."* WR340 is S-band; it physically cannot reach 9.2 GHz.
- **The topology is the opposite.** *"therefore does not have a reflective backplane… an absorber/transmitter rather than an absorber/reflector."* It also requires soldered lumped resistors and capacitors. Example 3 is a mirror-backed, fully-printed absorber/reflector.

**A mildly informative negative:** Gu independently lands on Landy's 17 µm copper — standard half-ounce cladding. That makes the patent's 0.15 mm look *more* anomalous, not less, which slightly strengthens #232's surviving hypothesis without corroborating it.

---

## 3. Ghosh — excluded, and it is the closest of the three

**Ghosh, Bhattacharyya, Kaiprath & Srivastava**, "Bandwidth-enhanced polarization-insensitive microwave metamaterial absorber and its equivalent circuit model," *J. Appl. Phys.* **115**(10), 104503 (2014). DOI [10.1063/1.4868577](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4868577). IIT Kanpur.

**Publisher-deposited abstract and 31-item reference list; no full text** (see §5). Verbatim from the abstract, `LITERATURE-SUPPORTED`:

> "The basic structure consists of **concentric rings embedded one inside another**… Simulation results show that the structure has enhanced bandwidth response with **full width at half maxima (FWHM) of 1.15 GHz (9.40–10.55 GHz)** with two absorption peaks at **9.66 and 10.26 GHz** (96% and 92.5% absorptivity, respectively)."

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Peak near 9.2 GHz? | **No.** Nearest peak 9.66 GHz, **+5.0%** |
| Metallisation | **Unknown** — behind the paywall |
| Shared dimensions | **No at topology level.** Nested concentric rings have no `a1`/`a2` to match against Example 3's rectangular ERR plus straight wire. Numbers unread |
| Cites Landy? | **Yes**, ref 3 of 31 (`10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.207402`) |

**This is the only one of the three that operates in X-band at all, so it deserves the sharper argument.** Two independent exclusions:

- **9.2 GHz is 0.20 GHz *below* the lower half-power edge.** At 9.2 GHz this device is below half its peak absorption — while FIG. 7G shows near-complete absorption there. The band does not merely miss; it disagrees about behaviour. `CALCULATED` from the stated FWHM.
- **Different device class.** Concentric nested rings versus ERR-plus-wire-resonator.

**Ghosh also cites Gu** (ref 29, `10.1063/1.3485808`). Two of the three cite each other, which reads as a topical cluster rather than a design lineage.

---

## 4. Singh — excluded, the expected miss

**Singh, Korolev, Afsar & Sonkusale**, "Single and dual band 77/95/110 GHz metamaterial absorbers on flexible polyimide substrate," *Appl. Phys. Lett.* **99**(26), 264101 (2011). DOI [10.1063/1.3672100](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3672100). Tufts University.

Publisher-deposited abstract and 19-item reference list; no full text.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Peak near 9.2 GHz? | **No.** *"Measured peak absorptions… are 92, 94, and 99% at 77.2, 94.8, and 109.5 GHz"*. Lowest is **8.4× above** 9.2 GHz |
| Metallisation | Not stated — but *"The total thickness of the absorber is just 126 μm"*, and Example 3's metallisation **alone** is 150 µm. Arithmetically impossible |
| Shared dimensions | **No.** Example 3's smallest listed dimension (0.6 mm) is 4.8× Singh's entire stack |
| Cites Landy? | **Yes**, ref 1 — the paper's first citation |

**Polyimide note, deliberately not carried further:** no permittivity or loss tangent was obtainable. Korolev and Afsar are from Tufts' High-Frequency Materials Measurement Center, so the full text is unusually likely to state one — but any value would be at 77–110 GHz and **would not transfer** to the repo's X-band Kapton 500HN figure of tanδ 0.012 ± 0.004. Flagged for `xband-absorber-substrate-shortlist.md` only if institutional access ever appears.

## 5. What could not be fetched, named

**A claim about the world:** *J. Appl. Phys.* (Ghosh) and *Appl. Phys. Lett.* (Singh) have **no free legal copy anywhere**. Three indexes converge — Unpaywall (`is_oa: false`, `has_repository_copy: false`, `oa_locations: []`), OpenAlex (`best_oa_location: null`, `any_repository_has_fulltext: false`), Semantic Scholar (`CLOSED`). Their full texts are a **purchasing decision, not a research one**.

**Claims about us**, all named: AIP article pages 403 to both WebFetch and curl (Cloudflare); ResearchGate 403 and not pursued regardless (third-party re-host, not a primary source); CORE, Scilit, Internet Archive Scholar, fatcat, DOAJ, OSTI, arXiv, institutional repositories and author pages — each tried and each empty or blocked. Semantic Scholar `/references` returned null and `/paper/search` rate-limited. The DukeSpace front-end sits behind an anti-bot proof-of-work challenge; Gu was routed around it via OAI-PMH and the DSpace REST API rather than defeating it.

**What that leaves open:** Ghosh's and Singh's metallisation thicknesses and dimension tables (Q2 and Q3) are unread. Neither could change the verdict — both papers are excluded on frequency and topology, which the abstracts settle — but the record should say they are unread rather than imply they were checked.

---

## 6. The `ε₀` / `ε₀ε_r` side-check: negative

Ghosh's title carries *"and its equivalent circuit model"*, so #246 asked whether it restates Costa's thin-spacer capacitance correction and with which prefactor — which would break the 2013-vs-2021 tie in [#234](https://github.com/parthalon025/Principle_RF_Engineer_Agent/issues/234).

**It does not cite Tretyakov & Simovski 2003.** All 31 publisher-deposited references were scanned for `tretyakov`, `simovski`, `costa`, `luukkonen`, `floquet`, `impedance surface` and `frequency selective` — **zero hits**, cross-checked by resolving 29 of the 31 individually through OpenAlex. There is nothing from the artificial-impedance-surface or grid-impedance literature at all. 30 of 31 slots are accounted for; entry 31 is an empty deposit slot, the only place a hidden citation could sit.

**And it almost certainly does not restate the correction** — an inference, not a reading, since the equivalent-circuit section is behind the paywall. The correction is never stated un-attributed in this literature (Costa 2013 cites [35] in the same sentence; Costa & Borgese 2021 likewise). The group's open-access sibling paper (Bhattacharyya, Ghosh & Srivastava, *AIP Advances* **4**, 097127) describes their model as a lumped per-ring RLC ladder — **a different modelling tradition** from Costa/Tretyakov's homogenised grid impedance with Floquet corrections. The correction has no natural place in that picture, which explains the citation absence cleanly.

**#234 is unchanged.** Its only remaining routes are Tretyakov & Simovski 2003 itself (closed access, no repository copy — `RUNNING-LISTS.md` §1) or a full-wave cross-check.

---

## 7. The records failure

`example3-inventor-publications.md` recorded author lists for all three papers under the label **"Cited verbatim from the patent's References Cited."** The patent prints only *"Gu et al."*, *"Ghosh et al."*, *"Singh et al."* — **no author lists at all**, at either line 83 or line 1022.

| Paper | Recorded | Actual (Crossref) |
|---|---|---|
| Gu | Gu, Chen, Zhang, Xu, Ma, Wang, Zhang & Zhao | **Gu, Barrett, Hand, Popa & Cummer** |
| Ghosh | …**Chaurasiya**… | …**Kaiprath**… |
| Singh | Singh, Tyler, Zhang, Azad & Chen | **Singh, Korolev, Afsar & Sonkusale** |

Titles, journals, volumes, issues, pages and years were all correct. **Only the authors — the one field the patent never supplied — were wrong.** Full account and the lesson: `RUNNING-LISTS.md` §3 correction **44**.

---

## 8. What this means

**For #116 (which curve to score against).** Nothing changes. The reproduction is still scored against the patent's `INFERRED` 9.2 GHz per #142's recommendation. This ticket closed the last cheap route to explaining the discrepancy by reading.

**For #232 (the metallisation-thickness solve).** It is now **the only remaining route**, and it is no longer optional as an alternative to reading. Mildly strengthened: Gu independently uses 17 µm on FR4, so 0.15 mm is anomalous against the field, not just against Landy.

**For #142.** Its finding stands, with one characterisation corrected: the three citations are **not** positioned as the design's source (§1). Its core result — the gap is real, 19.9%, and unexplained — is untouched.

**A new observation, weak but worth recording.** All three cited papers cite Landy; Gu's authors are Landy's own Duke ECE department; the patent adopts all three *"in their entireties."* The patent's own cited literature leads straight to Landy while its reference list omits him. That makes "the inventors had not encountered Landy" harder to sustain — but it is a claim about the citation graph, not about intent, and this document does not draw one.
